about.title: Ninety minutes. Nothing else.
about.lead: ninety is a scores site for people who just want to know what happened, what is happening, and what is next — in the competitions they actually follow.
about.why: The big scores sites have become hard to use: crowded pages, pop-ups, and a league table three taps away. We think a fan should open one page and see today’s matches, flip to yesterday or tomorrow in a single tap, and reach any table, squad or match in two.
about.why1: No adverts, no pop-ups, no cookie theatre.
about.why2: Six competitions followed properly instead of two hundred followed badly.
about.why3: Every score, table and squad reachable in two taps. Search with ⌘K.
about.why4: Light or dark, fast on a phone, readable at a glance, in English and Arabic.
about.testing: ninety is in testing. Scores, fixtures, tables and squads are live for the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A and the Champions League. Not yet: goal scorers, line-ups, the live minute clock, and the Europa League. Those arrive with the next data source.
about.feedback: If something looks wrong or you miss something, tell us.
about.dataTitle: How the data is kept right
about.data: ninety is built to never trust a single source. A sync pipeline pulls each fixture and result from a licensed data provider every fifteen minutes, normalises it into one model, and is designed to compare it field by field against a second provider as soon as one is connected.
about.step1t: Every configured provider is queried for the same competitions.
about.step2t: Team and player names are mapped to canonical identities, so “Man Utd”, “Manchester United FC” and “Manchester United” are one club.
about.step3t: When providers agree, the value is written with full confidence. When they disagree, the majority wins if there is one, and the disagreement is logged.
about.step4t: Remaining conflicts are handed to a Claude model with all the evidence. It returns a decision, a confidence and its reasoning, and anything below the confidence bar is held for a human.
about.step5t: League tables and scorer charts are computed from the results stored here, so a table can never disagree with the results you can click on.
about.demoNote: Deployments that show a Demo data badge run on a synthetic season generated for development: real clubs and competitions, but fictional results, squads and players.
about.name: A match lasts ninety minutes. The mark is a pitch seen from above: the halfway line, the centre circle, the spot where every game starts. The prime after the name is the minute mark on a match clock — 90′.
